facts.statement: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan agreed in Almaty on 18 February 1992 to keep the water allocations already in force and set up the Interstate Commission for Water Coordination; Afghanistan is not a party.
facts.source: Agreement on cooperation in the joint management, use and protection of interstate water resources, 18 February 1992 (text kept by the University of Texas at Austin)

facts.statement: Tajikistan started the first unit of the Rogun hydropower plant on the Vakhsh in November 2018.
Afghanistan’s authorities began building the Qosh Tepa canal from the Amu Darya in March 2022.
facts.source: Office of the First Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Afghanistan (de facto authorities): The First Deputy Prime Minister traveled to Balkh to inaugurate the Qosh Tepa Canal
